HTC caught storing fingerprints AS WORLD-READABLE CLEARTEXT

Biometrics should be thought of as usernames, not passwords because they are not secret. Software producers need to start treating them as such.

"HTC caught storing usernames AS WORLD-READABLE CLEARTEXT" is a lot less alarmist.

Absolutely incorrect. Biometrics need better security than passwords. Passwords can be easily changed. Biometrics require extensive surgery to change. It is possible to take a fingerprint biometric template and recreate a fingerprint that will fool most systems. This is a major issue if their fingerprint sensor and image processing technology is any good.

The very fact that biometrics cannot be changed renders them unsuitable for use as passwords.

This is why they, at best, can serve as usernames. The secrets that guard user data must be changeable, because at some point, someone's secret WILL be compromised and re-securing the system will require using a new secret. Would anyone take seriously the security of a system where you were unable to change your password, even after it was compromised? Of course not.

Biometrics don't fit the bill for use as passwords.

Specifically regarding fingerprints, you leave these ALL OVER, for anyone to find. Do you do this with passwords? Heck no! But usernames...? Much more so
That's why good security systems use a minimum of 2 factors. Fingerprints are one factor.
That's still like saying usernames are one factor for authentication.
They are: usernames are part of the factor "what you know". Fingerprints are part of the factor "who you are".
Usernames are, and should be treated as, public knowledge, and thus isn't a factor when it comes to security.
So you're saying usernames shouldn't be a part of security? I'll disagree with that.

I wasn't arguing they should be used as passwords. They are something different and should be their own thing. However you shouldn't be letting the template of a well-captured fingerprint out for anyone to capture like you would with a username. That's a Very Bad Idea.
